page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The allocation provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores utilizing 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and FMA.

Memory capacity is set to 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding an unusually dense 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage, requiring attached network block storage for persistence. Network connectivity operates with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Acceleration hardware is not present, with the instance providing zero physical or virtual GPUs.

Benchmark measurements position the processing and throughput capabilities of this instance primarily in the lower tiers of comparable cloud hardware. The CPU registers a stress-ng multi-core score of 2935.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2207.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 20.87 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 18.81 GB/sec. Data manipulation tasks reflect these limits, showing single-threaded gzip compression at 19.26 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.88 GB/sec. Application benchmarks record Redis SET operations at 2.88 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 3.47 GB/sec.

The restricted memory pool of 4.0 GB relative to 4 vCPUs creates a clear architectural tradeoff, rendering the instance unsuitable for memory-demanding applications or medium-to-large language models. However, it delivers dedicated compute execution with vectorized AVX-512 instruction support for smaller compute footprints. Cost efficiency is maximized in horizontally scalable batch environments, lightweight network proxying, basic microservices, and compute-focused tasks that require minimal working memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance offering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without integrated local storage or hardware GPU acceleration. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps. Empirical benchmarks indicate entry-level compute throughput, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 2935.19, Geekbench multi-core score of 2207.0, and static web serving throughput of 3.47 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains constrained, reaching 20.87 GB/sec on uncached reads. Given the small memory capacity, the instance is engineered for lightweight CPU-bound processes, small-scale batch automation, and utility microservices with minimal in-memory data requirements.
